_comment: 8-hart + IME demo stack for the sensor-demo mp4 Gantt. Every lane maps to a real sensor path in the flying drone demo (record_sensor_demo.py, FusedSensorNet warehouse gate weave): mlp_control = state-estimate -> motor commands (CTRL); fused_full = FPV greyscale CNN + cross-ToF conv + low-dim state -> LSTM -> velocity command (the sensor-fusion NAV net, the core of the demo); yolov8_nano_64x96 = FPV greyscale -> gate/person boxes (the YOLO panel); ffn_block + attn_block = a goal-conditioned vision-transformer head over the FPV image tokens (M=128 linears above the measured M=10.1 IME/RVV crossover -> the dispatches an impl-aware solve moves onto the cluster-0 MAC unit). The transformer pair is a ViNT-class STAND-IN until ViNT itself is compiled (coordination/k1_hil/requests_to_a/009). enable_impls gives every dispatch an rvv_x60 and ime_x60 cost cell; IME combinations exist only on CPU_P#0-3 (harts 0-3 run smt.vmadot; 4-7 SIGILL), enforced in xpu-rt/capabilities.py. Instance counts are tuned to one compact hyperperiod (~190 ops) so MOSEK converges to a balanced, optimal placement that loops cleanly under the flying drone. dronet was dropped: it is a redundant camera net not in the flying loop, so it weakened the 'directly tied to the demo' story.
_machines_comment: cpu_p:4 + cpu_e:4 = 8 distinct scheduler lanes. IME is offered only on the 4 CPU_P (cluster-0) lanes, which is physically faithful. For a real board (HIL) run cluster1 still needs a distinct core-kind so CPU_E#n does not alias onto harts 0-3; that is deferred and out of scope for the Gantt.
_topo_comment: topo_tag_override=true pins every machine combination to the single-core profile. singletons + topo_0 must go together: a multi-hart timing here would credit each core with the whole cluster's throughput.
